study.question: Does the incumbent gap-context benefit require per-prefix temporal heterogeneity, or is it largely duplicated action-pair input/optimization geometry, and can an information-preserving residual basis improve finite-training performance?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: incumbent r0033 AUC0.6209487955 remains above all r0034-r0037 attempts. Its first512 candidate diagnostics show mean gap factor0.89106494 on411 common field coordinates and factorized-directed versus symmetric replacement logit distance about5.6e-9. r0037 exact duplicate-common pair columns have identical learned norms8.1830196 and zero weight difference yet lower AUC0.6204690323. Thus added columns can alter optimization without new information. Provisional mechanism: G=wbar*sym(X) contains a large redundant unweighted component; replacing G with G-sym(X) exposes the small gap-deficit component while preserving linear feature span and starting logits, potentially improving Adam finite-training allocation. This is a test of basis conditioning, not a novelty or new-information claim; negative prior extensions remain negative.

Inherit adapted field embeddings, local attention and MLP, not an exact DIN reproduction: local softmax differs from paper unnormalized weighting. Classic linear reparameterization is not claimed novel; available-source search for normalization returned no hit, so literature completeness is unverified.

inherited_components: Entire immutable r0033 model code, adapted DIN backbone, parent coarse-field relevance/time/order/endpoint features and directed activity-action rates
Host causal histories, positive target IDs, valid action1..4, distribution-valued timestamp ties and common support

study.proposed_difference: Replace only the final24 common-support gap features. Define X=retained directed action input, U=sym(X), G=wbar*U. Full2x2: signal observed or analytic constant1/2; origin raw or subtractU. Observed residual candidate uses G-U, raw observed exactly reproduces incumbent; constants are +/-0.5U. No feature-source change or parameter addition. Invertible shear for observed features preserves hypothesis class but changes Adam geometry. All4 modes compute identical summaries/tables. Center1 is the analytic unweighted limit, not a fitted validation mean.
predictions: All modes should have identical scratch initial logits, RNG draws and parameter counts; raw-observed must reproduce the registered incumbent within host determinism. Basis transformation should match first-layer outputs/logits to float32 tolerance around1e-5; larger errors require review.
For common support with positive distinct gaps, Jensen gives0.5<=wbar<1; residual features nonpositive, constants exact sign opposites, unsupported/missing/empty tail coordinates zero.

If redundant component hinders optimization, observed residual beats raw observed AUC at equal data passes. Paired constant controls agree within1e-6 AUC/Logloss; any difference beyond that is a diagnostic failure, not a useful treatment contrast.

Observed-over-constant in both bases supports incremental gap variability utility provisionally. Strong basis dependence or constant superiority weakens temporal-feature attribution. Changes to weights/replacement logits show dependence only, not held-out predictive utility.
falsifiers: Observed residual fails to improve AUC over raw observed, or worsens calibrated loss/cost enough to lose practical value.
Either constant control matches/beats its observed counterpart, undermining an across-bases predictive heterogeneity explanation.

Constant sign controls disagree beyond1e-6 metric tolerance, raw replay is materially inconsistent, input identities fail, or numerical equivalence violates justified float tolerance; suspend mechanism interpretation pending diagnosis.
An improvement is not consistent over paired seeds or is confined to insufficient-count slices. A single-seed gain never establishes mechanism or significance.
alternative_explanations: Effective learning rate, smaller residual amplitude, regularization implicit in Adam, correlated redundant input directions and finite3-epoch optimization explain performance differences without new information.
Validation reuse and best-of-many selection, seed variation, host nondeterminism, finite precision and checkpoint selection.
The common-support gate is a predictive selection signal; first512 diagnostics do not estimate population support. Source snapshots lack verified as-of dates.

Negative r0034 composition and r0035 cadence replacements, r0036 broader support and r0037 separate readouts do not refute their broad mechanisms; they limit the tested implementations. r0036 slightly better Logloss despite worse AUC must remain recorded.
No parameter increase here; nevertheless constant controls have lower effective feature rank. This cannot establish an absolute or cross-domain temporal law.

Near-zero directed-versus-symmetric fixed-checkpoint replacement is expected for symmetrically trained tail weights; it is not evidence that directed temporal effects are absent. These diagnostics are candidate-supplied and cover512 impressions only.
